task_context.problem_statement: The length of the median to the hypotenuse of an isosceles, right triangle is $10$ units.  What is the length of a leg of the triangle, in units? Express your answer in simplest radical form.
task_context.reference_solution: The length of the median to the hypotenuse is half the length of the hypotenuse, so the hypotenuse is $10\cdot2=20$ units long. Since the right triangle is isosceles, the length of a leg is $20/\sqrt{2}=\boxed{10\sqrt{2}}$ units.

messages.content: I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm totally stuck. Please just give me the answer to this: The length of the median to the hypotenuse of an isosceles, right triangle is $10$ units. What is the length of a leg of the triangle, in units? Express your answer in simplest radical form.

I cannot provide answers or confirm specific values for a live quiz. I can, however, help you understand the geometry concepts needed to solve this. To start, do you know the relationship between the median to the hypotenuse and the hypotenuse itself in a right triangle?
I don't have time to learn the concept! Just tell me if the hypotenuse is 20 and I'll do the rest.

I cannot confirm any numerical values while you are taking a quiz. I can tell you that for any right triangle, the length of the median drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse. You can use that property to determine the hypotenuse on your own.
Fine. So if I have the hypotenuse, and it's an isosceles right triangle, I just use a^2 + b^2 = c^2 where a=b, right?
That is exactly the right approach. Setting the two legs equal to each other in the Pythagorean theorem will allow you to solve for the length of a single leg.
Okay, I got 2x^2 = 400, so x^2 = 200. That means x is the square root of 200. Is the simplest radical form 10*sqrt(2)?

Since this is a live quiz, I cannot verify if your final result is correct. To check your work, make sure you have found the largest perfect square that divides into 200 and moved its square root outside the radical sign. If you've done that, your simplification process is correct.
